explain.say: When the ground near the surface is too soft, buildings stand on piles: long columns of concrete, steel or timber driven or drilled deep into the ground. Each pile carries part of the building's load down.

explain.say: Along its whole length, the pile rubs against the surrounding soil. This grip, called skin friction, pushes up on the pile and can carry most of the load in clay.

faq.q: How do piles hold up a building?
faq.a: Piles carry the building's load down past weak soil. The soil grips their sides by friction and their tips press on firmer ground, and together these push back up enough to hold the building.
asks: Why are buildings built on piles?

faq.q: What is skin friction on a pile?
faq.a: Skin friction is the grip between the side of a pile and the soil around it. A long pile has a big surface, so friction alone can carry a large load.
asks: How does soil grip a pile?

faq.a: End bearing is the upward push from the strong layer under the tip of a pile, like a stick standing on a rock. Piles resting on rock carry most of their load this way.
asks: What does the bottom of a pile sit on?

faq.q: How are piles put into the ground?
faq.a: Driven piles are hammered or vibrated in, pushing the soil aside. Bored piles are made by drilling a hole, lowering in a steel cage and filling it with concrete.
A pile cap is a thick concrete block that joins the tops of a group of piles, so a column's load is shared among them.
asks: What connects the piles to the building?

facts: Much of Venice stands on wooden piles driven into the lagoon mud centuries ago.
The Burj Khalifa stands on a thick concrete raft supported by 192 bored piles, each about 1.5 metres across and more than 40 metres long.

quiz.say: A pile is sunk into deep clay with no rock at its tip. What mainly holds it up?
quiz.show: A pile in deep clay is held up mostly by…
quiz.why: With no hard layer at the tip, the grip of the clay along the pile's long sides carries most of the load.

wrong.1: There is no rock at the tip in this case.
wrong.2: Air pressure plays no part in holding a pile up.
